units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Arrived. It looks like a normal house.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: From the outside, it does. But this is one of the most important buildings in the history of printing.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a World Heritage Site, listed in 2005.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A house?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A house, a workshop and a printing business, all together.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The family lived above and printed below, for about four centuries.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Four hundred years in one building.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Plantin moved in in 1576. After he died, his son-in-law Jan Moretus took over the business, and the Moretus family kept it going, generation after generation.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Until when?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1876, Edward Moretus sold the company to the city of Antwerp.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And a year later, in 1877, the public could visit the living rooms and presses.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So it has been a museum for nearly 150 years.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Over 140, yes. Now, here is the headline.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The museum holds the two oldest surviving printing presses in the world.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The oldest in the world. In Antwerp.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In a house on a market square.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Not in a grand hall.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What else is in there?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A Gutenberg Bible, the 36-line one.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the rooms where the family lived and worked.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So it's a time capsule.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A very good one. And there's a courtyard garden, so even if you're short on time, it's a calm place to stand for a minute.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Why was a printer so important to Antwerp?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Because in the 16th century, Antwerp was a place where ideas and goods and money moved fast.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Printing is the same business.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You make something, you send it far.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A bit like the port.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A paper port. Books left Antwerp the way pepper and cloth did.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And what's the link to Rubens?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: This is the thread we promised.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Resurrection of Christ in the cathedral was painted as a memorial for Jan Moretus.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: So the painter and the printer worked in the same circle of the same city.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Good. The printing house, the painter, the church.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: All connected.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: One city, one small world.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Practical?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: This is an indoor stop, so it's your rain plan.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Check the opening hours and ticket details before you go.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a place where you could spend an hour or more if you read the labels.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And I should stay under an hour, I guess, because of the schedule.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: If you're short on time, go for the presses, the printing room, and the courtyard.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wait. A thought. The first printers made their letters by hand.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: They cut them in metal, they set them by hand, they pulled the press by hand.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And you're counting it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Tally says four. Including that one.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: I'm not sure that's what the bet meant.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The bet said hands. I'm just being generous.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Pause here. Go in if you can.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And then, the last stop?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Walk east, toward the shopping street called the Meir.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's about 10 minutes on foot.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Rubens House is just off it, on a short street called the Wapper.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: If you lose the way, ask for the Rubenshuis.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Everybody knows it.
